card.title: Who Changed It?
card.instruction: Ask innocent questions until someone admits altering the plan, schedule, arrangement, or shared space.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can't open the cupboard. Was the sofa this close yesterday?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's more room for yoga now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Did making that room involve moving the sofa?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes, I moved it. I put the things you'll need somewhere easier.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How thoughtful. Would those be the mugs in your sock drawer, or has someone else improved the kitchen too?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 mild cupboard question probes changed layout, A3 elicits sofa movement and A5 extends innocent inquiry to displaced kitchen objects.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 yoga space causes A3 direct-but-calm movement question; B4 admission and easier storage claim cause A5 sock-drawer inquiry.

relationship.evidence: B2 gives the improvement rationale and B4 admits the change while offering another helpful explanation.

heightening.evidence: B4 admission does not end A's investigation because the claimed relocated things cause A5 a next concrete alteration question.

specificity.evidence: A1 blocked cupboard and B2 yoga room establish a shared-space change with practical consequences.
